- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility.
- Overestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum or mean reversion.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends — forecasts dip too early or too slowly.
- Overreacts to recent price spikes, overshooting the true value by 5–15% in the immediate aftermath.
- Underestimates mean-reversion periods — fails to recognize when prices are likely to return to historical averages after a spike.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values in the first 10 days of the forecast, especially when historical prices are trending upward.
- When true prices rise sharply, model often fails to capture the full magnitude — underestimates the peak and then overcorrects later.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history includes recent volatility — model performs worse when history is flat or trending downward.
